clue.text: Nothing drunk by a poet ready to set sail

indicators.note: something drunk by another is taken inside it, so the zero goes within the poet phrase

parts.note: a bard is a poet
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A poet with an empty glass is all set to go on a voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: Passengers who are on the ship are ready for it to set sail, so the word suits a vessel about to depart.

clue.text: Spots men carting bottles up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top
the phrase men carting bottles, or holds, the letters within it

explanation.surface: Workmen are hauling crates of bottles uphill.
explanation.definitionFit: A skin condition marked by pimples is what spots means here.

clue.text: Remote land available for purchase in reserve

parts.note: a product that is out has been released and can be bought
a back-up is something held in reserve, so back covers it

explanation.surface: Land for sale is held back as a reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: The remote, sparsely populated interior of Australia is called by this name.

clue.text: Scour island for shooter

parts.note: to rifle through something is to search or scour it
the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: Searching an island for a gunman.
explanation.definitionFit: An infantry soldier armed with a long gun is a marksman or shooter.

clue.text: Given additional quality by Nutmeg?

parts.note: Nutmeg is the setter's pseudonym and also a spice, so anything she flavours has been enlivened with spice

explanation.surface: The setter boasts that her puzzle has been improved by her own touch.
explanation.walkthrough: Nutmeg is the name this setter uses, so the clue is both self-praise and a cookery note: food with nutmeg added has literally had spice put in.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something livelier or more interesting is the idiom for adding extra quality, just as spice enlivens a dish.

clue.text: Shipping line's carrying artillery to fight source of evil

indicators.note: the shipping line's letters carry the artillery inside them

parts.note: P&O is a famous British shipping line, here with its possessive S
RA is the Royal Artillery
to box is to fight

explanation.surface: A ferry company transports guns for a war.
explanation.walkthrough: P&O (Peninsular and Oriental) is a British ferry and cruise company; the ampersand is read as AND.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the jar opened by the first woman released all the ills of the world, hence any source of trouble.

clue.text: Obscure brash Yankee about to take the lead

indicators.note: the letter for about goes in front, taking the lead over the rest

parts.note: C, for circa, means about
loud can mean brash or showy
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A boastful American is about to go into first place unnoticed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something murky or unclear is obscure, as cloudy water hides what lies beneath.

clue.text: Yearned to possess sink

parts.note: to be dying for something is to yearn for it
to own is to possess

explanation.surface: Someone longed to own a kitchen sink.
explanation.definitionFit: To subside or lessen gradually, as wind does, is to sink in intensity.

clue.text: Charlie feeding writer German fare

indicators.note: the word for Charlie is fed into the word for writer

parts.note: a pen is a writing tool
a charlie is British slang for a fool, an ass

explanation.surface: Someone serves a writer some German food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fare' looks like food, but a fare is a paying traveller, as in a taxi's fare.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi driver's fare is the person paying to ride, a traveller carried for money.

clue.text: Keep informed of tiny changes

indicators.note: the words 'of tiny' change, meaning their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be told about every small change.
explanation.definitionFit: To advise someone formally of news is to inform them, so the verb fits keeping a person updated.

clue.text: Hinders second examiner's case, cutting corners

indicators.note: the examiner's outer letters cut into the word for corners, splitting it

parts.note: nooks are corners

indicators.note: a case is the outside of something, so only the first and last letters of examiner are kept

parts.note: the possessive ending only links the case to the examiner

explanation.surface: An examiner's work is hampered when a second case is handled with shortcuts.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker, leaving an opponent with no clear shot obstructs them, so the verb has come to mean hampers or thwarts.

clue.text: Head deity's mantle encapsulating old belief

parts.note: a cape is a mantle, a sleeveless cloak

indicators.note: the phrase for the deity's encloses the abbreviation for old, like a capsule

parts.note: the deity's mantle is the mantle of God
hope is a belief or expectation

explanation.surface: A chief god's cloak is said to wrap up some ancient faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a chief or leader but is a headland, here the famous promontory at the southern tip of Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A head is a headland jutting into the sea, and this South African promontory is one of the most famous.

clue.text: First non-medallist reportedly approaching with plenty to say

indicators.note: means the word is as heard, so it sounds like the word wanted

parts.note: the first competitor to miss a medal finishes fourth
coming means approaching

explanation.surface: The athlete who just missed the podium is reported to be talking freely.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone forthcoming is open and willing to share information, so talkative.

clue.text: Presume army reservists are asked to reassemble

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: the letters are put together again in a different order

explanation.surface: Reserve soldiers are told to gather again at the depot.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army (TA) was the name of the British Army's part-time reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept something without needing proof is to assume it, so the phrase means presume.

clue.text: Schedule daily cold drink

parts.note: The Times is a daily newspaper
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
ale is a drink

explanation.surface: Each day's schedule includes a chilled drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A planned period for completing stages of work is a timetable or schedule.

clue.text: Game partners try turning over to canoodle

parts.note: in the card game bridge, South and North are partners

indicators.note: the word for try is turned over, so read backwards

parts.note: to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: A couple at a game have another attempt before flipping a card and cuddling.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge is played by two partnerships, North-South and East-West, so S and N are partners.
explanation.definitionFit: Kissing and cuddling amorously is the British slang sense of the definition.

clue.text: Goalie maybe put off guarding goal

indicators.note: the word for put off surrounds the goal, guarding it

parts.note: to defer is to postpone or put off
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper delays things while protecting the net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goal' looks like a football net but is an end, an aim.
explanation.definitionFit: A goalkeeper is one example of a player whose job is to protect against attack.

clue.text: See 24
Pasture with fine mature greenery

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or pasture
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: A field with good, well-grown vegetation.
explanation.definitionFit: Foliage collectively, the leaves of plants, is green vegetation.

clue.text: A brother we shot in turn-of-century conflict

indicators.note: the letters of 'A brother we' are shot to pieces and rearranged

explanation.surface: A sibling and the speaker were wounded in a battle around 1900.
explanation.definitionFit: The war between Britain and the Afrikaner republics ran from 1899 to 1902, straddling the change of century.

clue.text: Tetchy self-righteous son occupying shower?

indicators.note: the pieces occupy the inside of the shower word

parts.note: a wash can be a shower, the question mark flagging the loose sense
pi is short for pious, self-righteous

explanation.surface: A smug son hogging the bathroom gets short-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: Irritable and quick to sting, like the insect, is the sense of this adjective.

clue.text: Asian from India pursuing desire to throttle setter

indicators.note: the letter for India pursues, coming after, the rest
the word for desire grips the setter by the throat, surrounding it

parts.note: a yen is a desire
the setter refers to herself as me
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone from India longs to strangle the puzzle's compiler.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from the Arabian state at the south-west of the peninsula is from Asia.

clue.text: Don't stint, inserting late pound in meagre bill

parts.note: spare can mean meagre or scanty

indicators.note: the words for late and pound are put inside the word for bill

parts.note: a bird's bill is its beak, slang for nose
ex means former or late
a pen is an enclosure, a pound for animals

explanation.surface: A late payment in sterling is added to a small invoice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' looks like an invoice, but here it is a beak, and so a nose.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay whatever it costs is the idiom for being lavish, the opposite of stinting.

clue.text: Jet from Bluegrass State arrived first

indicators.note: the word for arrived comes first, before the state

parts.note: a train that is in has arrived
Kentucky, nicknamed the Bluegrass State, is abbreviated KY

explanation.surface: A plane from Kentucky landed ahead of schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jet' looks like an aircraft but is the black colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Jet is an intensely black stone, and something dark like spilt writing fluid is black.

clue.text: Self-help group covering roughly half the folk on campus

indicators.note: the group's letters surround the other pieces, covering them

parts.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous, a self-help organisation
ca, short for circa, means roughly
demi is a prefix meaning half

explanation.surface: A support group's meeting includes about half the townspeople.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholars and university staff collectively make up the world of higher learning found on a campus.

clue.text: One admiral at sea a regular record keeper

indicators.note: something at sea is confused, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A naval officer on a voyage keeps a ship's log faithfully.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram covers both 'One' and 'admiral'; the answer is Sue Townsend's teenage diarist, whose secret diary was a bestseller.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional schoolboy kept a diary he wrote in daily, so he is a regular keeper of records.

clue.text: Extremely gregarious dogs still at home when light fades?

indicators.note: to dog someone is to follow them, so these letters come after the rest

parts.note: even can mean still, as in 'even better'
in means at home

indicators.note: the extremes of gregarious are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Sociable dogs stay indoors when daylight goes.
explanation.definitionFit: The later part of each day, after sunset and before night, is the time the daylight dims.

clue.text: Leading lady cleared out in cunning fashion

parts.note: arch means chief or leading, as in archenemy

indicators.note: the word lady has its insides cleared out, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: The star actress was turfed out by some crafty manoeuvre.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a knowing, mischievous or sly manner is the adverb's sense, close to cunningly.
